Office Visit - Follow-up
Patient: Jonas Fairbanks | DOB: 10/22/1983 | MRN: SYN-2874379
Date of service: 03/20/2025 | Dr. Henrik Bellamy, MD

History of present illness:
41-year-old man seen for follow-up of low back pain. He first noticed the pain shooting down his right leg after lifting a heavy box, nearly three months before this visit.

Treatment to date:
Two months of supervised exercise sessions plus over-the-counter anti-inflammatories have not brought lasting relief.

History:
Past medical history: type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia.
Medications: metformin 500 mg twice daily; atorvastatin 20 mg nightly.

Review of systems:
Red flag screen negative: denies bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, fever, unexplained weight loss, or history of cancer.

Physical exam:
Back: tenderness over the lower lumbar paraspinal muscles; straight-leg raise positive on the right at 40 degrees.
Neuro: strength 4/5 in right ankle dorsiflexion and great toe extension, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, decreased light touch over the dorsum of the right foot.

Assessment and plan:
Assessment: right L5 lumbar radiculopathy.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for disc herniation; home exercise program; follow up after imaging.
